kpis.description: Objective from a kp App master hire.
kpis.measure_config: {"appMaster":{"direction":"gte","kpiKey":"gate_pass_rate","windowDays":60},"source":"kp-app-master"}
kpis.name: gate pass rate
kpis.rationale: Seeded at App master hire from the kp AppMasterSpec objectives.

kpis.description: Objective from a kp App master hire.
kpis.measure_config: {"appMaster":{"direction":"gte","kpiKey":"proposal_merge_rate","windowDays":90},"source":"kp-app-master"}
kpis.name: proposal merge rate
kpis.rationale: Seeded at App master hire from the kp AppMasterSpec objectives.

kpis.description: Percentage of active twin channel slots (across all projects with a trained twin) configured with a connector other than 'manual'. A channel on 'manual' means every approved reply still requires copy-paste by the user; a real connector means the twin can deliver autonomously. This is the adoption signal that tells whether the twin is a draft aid or an actual communication agent.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Open /app/[any-trained-project]/sprava-kanalu, count enabled channels, count those with a non-manual connector configured. Repeat across a sample of 10 projects with resolved.source === 'trained'. Rate = real-connector channels / total enabled channels."}
kpis.name: Twin channel real-connector rate
kpis.rationale: If this stays near zero it means users train a voice but never connect it to a real channel — the twin is a drafting tool, not an autonomous agent, and the autonomy architecture built into `decideDraft` / `enforceAutonomy` has no practical reach.

kpis.description: Share of projects with the Kanály module that have at least one channel status saved as anything other than the default (not-started) state — i.e., the user has begun tracking outreach work against the plan.
kpis.measure_config: {"cmd":"node -e \"const {initLocalDb} = require('./src/lib/local-db'); (async()=>{const db=await initLocalDb(); const rows=await db.all(\\\"SELECT value FROM kv WHERE key LIKE 'organic-channels/%'\\\"); const total=rows.length; const engaged=rows.filter(r=>{try{const v=JSON.parse(r.value); return v.statuses && Object.values(v.statuses).some(s=>s!=='not-started');}catch{return false;}}).length; console.log(total===0?'N/A':(engaged/total*100).toFixed(1)+'%');})()\"","parse":"first line, strip %"}
kpis.name: Channel status engagement rate
kpis.rationale: A channel plan nobody acts on is decoration — this rate distinguishes projects where users are translating the ranked plan into real zero-spend outreach work from those where the module is view-only.

kpis.description: Percentage of real (non-demo) projects where the Sklad seasonal budget plan is grounded in actual trailing 30-day Ads spend rather than the notional 120,000 CZK fallback baseline.
kpis.measure_config: {"journey":"For a sample of 10 non-demo projects open /app/[id]/sklad-sezonnost; check whether the ModulePage `sample` gutter badge appears. Count pages WITHOUT the badge (real grounding) vs total."}
kpis.name: Sklad real-budget grounding rate
kpis.rationale: When the budget plan rests on the notional baseline the CZK recommendations are fictitious — a user acting on them mis-allocates real ad spend.

kpis.description: Share of authenticated workspaces that have created two or more projects, measured as an aggregate snapshot.
kpis.measure_config: {"pass_criteria":"Rate computed without error; record numerator and denominator separately","steps":["Count total distinct workspaces (users) with at least one project","Count those with project count ≥ 2","Rate = (≥2-project workspaces) / (all workspaces with ≥1 project)"]}
kpis.name: Multi-project workspace rate
kpis.rationale: A workspace managing two or more clients has crossed the retention threshold that distinguishes a committed agency user from a trial tourist — this rate is the stickiness signal this context directly enables.

kpis.description: Percentage of GBP post ideas in the ContentSchedule board that ultimately reach 'published' status, measuring full editorial funnel completion.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"For at least 3 projects, call GET /api/projects/{projectId}/state/content-schedule and parse the posts array. Compute published / (idea + scheduled + published). Exclude boards with 0 total posts.","sample_size":"3 projects with non-empty boards"}
kpis.name: GBP post idea-to-published conversion rate
kpis.rationale: Ideas that accumulate without ever being published indicate the GBP posting pipeline is stalled — silently undermining local SEO visibility while the board appears busy.

kpis.description: Share of active lead sources classified as 'junk' (low CPL but high CPQL, generating volume without qualified pipeline).
kpis.name: Lead junk-source rate
kpis.rationale: Rising junk-source share means budget is rewarding form count over qualified leads — the core mis-optimisation this module's warning banner flags.

kpis.description: Share of customer reviews in the ReviewInbox marked as answered, as tracked by the health strip's replyRate computation.
kpis.name: Review inbox response rate
kpis.rationale: The inbox health strip already flags reply rate below 50%; unanswered critical reviews directly erode reputation, feeding back into lead conversion quality.

kpis.description: Among projects where the automated client report cadence is set to anything other than 'off', the percentage that have at least one explicit recipient email address configured. When the recipients list is empty the system falls back to the account owner, meaning the actual client never receives the white-label report directly.
kpis.measure_config: {"journey":"Open ReportSettings for a sample of projects where cadence ≠ 'off'; check the recipients field. Count those with ≥1 email as passing. Report passing / total."}
kpis.name: Automated report client recipient fill rate
kpis.rationale: An empty recipients field silently redirects white-label reports to the agency owner — the client never sees them — so a low fill rate means the automated-delivery value proposition is unused even when cadence is configured.

kpis.description: Fraction of POST /api/ai calls that return HTTP 429 with code:"quota" due to the per-user aiEval daily limit, not the global ceiling.
kpis.measure_config: {"connector":"sentry","query":"Filter Sentry issues: url contains /api/ai AND http.status_code:429 AND message contains code:quota, divide count by total /api/ai event count in the same window."}
kpis.name: AI per-user daily quota saturation rate
kpis.rationale: Rising quota saturation means users are hitting their personal generation ceiling — a direct signal to raise plan limits or surface the upgrade path before they churn.

kpis.description: Percentage of inbound leads responded to within the configured SLA window (SLA_TARGET_MIN), as reported by the withinSlaRate field in computeResponseAnalytics.
kpis.measure_config: {"steps":"Open SpeedLeadModule with demo leads. Respond to each lead before its countdown reaches 0. Verify the 'Within SLA' analytics band shows ≥80%. Then let one lead breach and confirm it shows <100%. Record the displayed withinSlaRate value."}
kpis.name: Lead SLA compliance rate
kpis.rationale: SLA compliance is the entire reason this module exists — if leads are routinely breaching the target window, revenue is leaking before any campaign spend is questioned.

kpis.description: Percentage of lead replies sent using the AI-generated text (usingAi === true) rather than the deterministic draftReply fallback.
kpis.measure_config: {"steps":"Open SpeedLeadModule with an LLM key configured. For 10 demo leads, track how many agents click 'Generate AI reply' and send the AI output vs sending without generating. Record the ratio. Also verify that rejecting an AI reply (confirmReject path) increments the twin's rejection count shown in the 'learned' banner."}
kpis.name: Lead AI reply adoption rate
kpis.rationale: If agents never trigger AI generation in the leads inbox, the twin's voice never gets trained on this channel and the deterministic draft stays the permanent ceiling.

kpis.description: Percentage of POST /api/patterns/search calls that return semantic: true (Gemini-embedding path) rather than falling back to substring match. A drop to 0 means the paid semantic capability silently degrades without surfacing any error to the user.
kpis.measure_config: {"journey":"POST /api/patterns/search with query 'high CTR headline structure', inspect response field `semantic`. Pass = true, Fail = false (substring fallback active)."}
kpis.name: Pattern search semantic hit rate
kpis.rationale: The semantic ranking is the premium differentiator of pattern discovery; a misconfigured embedding key silently downgrades every search to substring with no user-visible signal.

kpis.description: Percentage of project diagnostic reports where the highest-ranked insight has 'strong' or 'weak' statistical significance rather than 'noise' or 'orientational'.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Open 10 recent project diagnostics in the app, note the significance tier of the first-listed insight in the Výkon/diagnostics panel; record the fraction where tier is 'strong' or 'weak'."}
kpis.name: Top insight significance rate
kpis.rationale: If the leading insight is always 'noise', compareInsightRank() is producing no ranking value and users are seeing statistically meaningless headlines at the top of the diagnostic card.

kpis.description: Percentage of non-demo projects that have a website domain configured in Project Settings. Domain is the seed for SEO scoring, keyword grounding, and local-SEO features; without it those operations fall back to demo data silently.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Navigate to /app/<project-id>/nastaveni for a sample of real (non-demo) projects. Count how many have a non-empty domain field. Divide by total real projects sampled."}
kpis.name: Project website domain fill rate
kpis.rationale: Domain is the linchpin for several AI operations (SEO brief, keyword research, local maps); a low fill rate means those modules silently run on generic data even for paying users.

kpis.description: Of all shared client report links created in the trailing 30 days, the percentage that recorded at least one view before expiry.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Query Firestore sharedReports collection; filter createdAt >= 30 days ago; count docs where views >= 1; divide by total. Report separately for expired vs active links."}
kpis.name: Shared client report view rate
kpis.rationale: If clients never open the link the white-label sharing feature delivers zero value — this is the most direct signal that campaign reports are actually reaching and being read by the end client.

kpis.description: Percentage of items in an uploaded or fetched feed that survive parsing and land in the catalog (not dropped for missing id+title or truncated by MAX_FEED_ITEMS).
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Upload a 500-item Heureka XML feed and a 500-item CSV feed to the import endpoint. Record diff.incoming vs (diff.added + diff.updated + diff.unchanged). Yield = (added+updated+unchanged) / incoming × 100."}
kpis.name: Feed import item yield rate
kpis.rationale: parseFeed silently truncates oversized feeds and drops rows without id+title — a low yield means users upload 500 SKUs and get 300 in their catalog with no prominent warning.

kpis.description: Percentage of POST /api/images responses where result.source equals 'leonardo' (real generation) rather than the placeholder-SVG fallback path that fires when the Leonardo API key is absent or the provider errors. Measured by a simulated generation journey that checks the response payload.
kpis.measure_config: {"steps":["POST /api/images with a short valid prompt, style=photo, format=square, count=1","Assert response status is 200","Assert response body field source === 'leonardo'","Record pass/fail; track 7-day rolling pass rate as the KPI value"]}
kpis.name: Image real-source rate
kpis.rationale: When Leonardo is unreachable or unconfigured, every generation silently returns placeholder SVGs and refunds the quota — users lose trust before any alert fires; this rate catches the outage first.

kpis.description: Percentage of generated briefs that score 70 or above on the built-in SEO scorecard (readability + keyword-coverage + E-E-A-T chips) computed by scoreBrief().
kpis.measure_config: {"prompt":"Sample 20 recent brief outputs from Firestore or LOCAL_DB. For each, call scoreBrief(result, result.primaryKeyword) from src/lib/content/seo-score.ts and record the `overall` field (0–100). Count the share where overall >= 70."}
kpis.name: Brief SEO overall score ≥70 rate
kpis.rationale: The SEO scorecard is the only automated quality gate on a generated brief; a low rate means most users receive briefs with visible red chips they must manually fix before the content is publishable.

kpis.description: % of change-sets that landed in 'applied' status where every individual move succeeded (results all ok=true). A set is partial-failed when status='applied' but okCount < moves.length.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"In Firestore, query all tenants/{tenant}/changeSets where status='applied' and results != null. For each, check if results.every(r => r.ok). Full-apply rate = (sets where all ok) / (total applied sets)."}
kpis.name: Change-set full-apply rate
kpis.rationale: A partial apply leaves the live ad account in a state the operator didn't intend — and since the change-set still reads 'applied', they may revert or report against it not realising only some moves took effect.

kpis.description: Share of local projects with live rank signals whose most-recent import (syncedAt) is within the past 35 days — one expected monthly cadence window. Stale-but-live projects have their outdated positions injected into the AI recap grounding text with a 'live data' tag.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"For each local project where resolveLocalLadder returns live:true, read meta.syncedAt from the local-signals store. Count the share where syncedAt >= now - 35d. Spot-check 5 projects per cycle."}
kpis.name: Rank signal freshness rate
kpis.rationale: A project that imported once and never again shows months-old rank positions in the monthly recap labeled as live data, giving the client false confidence in their current Google Maps standing.

kpis.description: Percentage of experiments marked 'done' whose visitor counts did not meet the required-per-arm sample-size threshold (hasEnoughData=false at close time), producing statistically untrustworthy winners that can pollute the patterns library.
kpis.measure_config: {"steps":"For each project with live experiments, list all items where status='done'. For each, re-run the evaluate() logic mentally or via the UI results panel: check if the progress bar reached 100% before being closed. Count done_before_gate / total_done."}
kpis.name: Experiment premature-close rate
kpis.rationale: A 'done' experiment that never cleared the trust gate produces a winner the Šidák math explicitly warns not to trust — and that winner is eligible to enter the AI prompt as an 'account-proven creative pattern'.

kpis.description: Share of critical inbox alerts created in the last 30 days that have advanced past 'new' status (acknowledged or resolved), measured across a sample of active tenants.
kpis.measure_config: {"prompt":"For 5 tenants that received a critical alert in the last 30 days, open their Firestore alerts collection, filter type=critical and createdAt within 30 days, count the fraction where status is 'acknowledged' or 'resolved' rather than 'new' (or missing)."}
kpis.name: Critical alert acknowledgement rate
kpis.rationale: The alert workflow added explicit acknowledged/resolved states; if operators never advance alerts out of 'new', the detection pipeline runs but produces no action — the inbox is decoration.

kpis.description: Of posts that entered the 'publishing' claim state in the last 7 days, the percentage that settled to 'published' rather than 'failed' or remaining stranded in 'publishing'.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Query tenant_docs collection 'social_posts' for records whose claimedAt is within the last 7 days. Count those with status='published' as successes; count status='failed' or status='publishing' with a claimedAt older than PUBLISH_CLAIM_TTL_MS (10 min) as failures. Rate = successes / (successes + failures) × 100."}
kpis.name: Scheduled post publish success rate
kpis.rationale: A failing post pipeline is invisible to users until they check manually — a drop below 95% means scheduled content is silently not going out on time.

kpis.description: Of all posts with status='published' in the last 30 days, the percentage where simulated !== true — i.e. the post actually reached a live social platform rather than returning a demo.social preview URL.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Query tenant_docs 'social_posts' for status='published'. Count records where simulated is false or absent (legacy real posts) as real; count where simulated=true as demo. Rate = real / total × 100."}
kpis.name: Real (non-simulated) publish rate
kpis.rationale: If this stays near 0% it means no user has real OAuth credentials wired up, so the entire publish pipeline is in permanent demo mode and delivering no actual social reach.

kpis.description: Fraction of project deletions where every satellite store (all 15 deleters + tenant Firestore scrub) completes without error — i.e. failed.length === 0 in the CascadeResult.
kpis.measure_config: {"query":"Search Sentry for events matching the message '[projects] delete cascade — partial failure' in the past 30 days; clean rate = 1 − (event count / total project deletions)."}
kpis.name: Cascade delete clean rate
kpis.rationale: A partial cascade leaves orphaned satellite data that is invisible, never auto-retried, and a GDPR/privacy liability — the context's single highest-stakes failure mode.

kpis.description: Of all analyzeAll batch runs (the 'evaluate everything' sweep that runs per-campaign + portfolio AI evals in one request), what percentage returned quotaExhausted=true — meaning the run completed only partially before hitting the AI quota ceiling.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Filter server logs or add telemetry on POST /api/campaigns/analyze/batch responses; count responses where quotaExhausted===true divided by total batch responses over the period."}
kpis.name: Batch eval quota-exhaustion rate
kpis.rationale: A rising quota-hit rate means large-portfolio accounts silently receive partial evaluations from a feature that presents itself as 'evaluate all' — the only signal without this KPI is a confused user whose remaining count never reaches zero.

kpis.description: % of projects older than 7 days where every type-appropriate onboarding step (scan, catalog, ads, ranks, channels, costModel as applicable) resolves to done=true in progress.ts
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Sample 50 projects created >7 days ago across project types; call resolveOnboardingProgress for each and record complete===true count divided by total sampled."}
kpis.name: Onboarding checklist full-completion rate
kpis.rationale: Distinct from activation rate — measures whether the wizard actually drives users all the way to live data, not just that they started; a low rate means grounded modules stay in demo mode.

kpis.description: % of projects where the onboarding state has dismissed=true but done < total steps, indicating the user closed the card before finishing setup
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Query onboarding store for all projects with dismissed=true; for each compute resolveOnboardingProgress and flag those with complete===false; report as % of all dismissed projects."}
kpis.name: Checklist dismissed-incomplete rate
kpis.rationale: A rising premature-dismiss rate is the earliest warning that the onboarding checklist UX is failing to motivate live-source connections before users tune it out.

kpis.description: Percentage of projects with an active warehouse connection whose provider is a real (non-demo) source — i.e. provider not in ['demo', 'erp-demo']. A project stuck on demo data gets no live stock, velocity, or COGS signals.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Query the connection store (Firestore collection inventory-connections or LOCAL_DB inventory_connections table). Count records where provider NOT IN ('demo','erp-demo') / total records × 100. Exclude rows with no connectedAt."}
kpis.name: Real warehouse connection rate
kpis.rationale: A project still on demo data gains nothing from the sync layer — this is the single cleanest signal that users trusted this subsystem with real credentials.

kpis.description: Percentage of active projects whose stored daily performance series meets or exceeds COVERAGE.fullMinDays (29 days, defined in src/lib/metrics/config.ts) so they receive full — not degraded or suppressed — anomaly and trend detection.
kpis.measure_config: {"check":"For each active project, load its daily performance series and evaluate seriesCoverage(series.length). Count projects where the result is 'full' and divide by the total number of active projects."}
kpis.name: Anomaly-detection eligible project rate
kpis.rationale: Projects below the 29-day threshold silently receive no anomaly alerts and no trend signals — users read an empty detection feed as 'all clear' rather than 'insufficient data', so this rate warns the operator before users escalate.

kpis.description: % of Google Ads sync attempts where getUserAccessToken returns a non-null token (either still-valid or successfully refreshed), indicating the user's Google session is intact and live data can flow.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Weekly: count '[google] token refresh failed' error events in Sentry (or server logs) against the number of Google-linked projects that attempted a sync. Rate = 1 - (failed_refreshes / sync_attempts_with_google_account)."}
kpis.name: Google Ads OAuth token freshness rate
kpis.rationale: This is the earliest warning that Google refresh tokens are expiring or being revoked at scale — it fires before 'Degraded campaign sync rate' because that metric captures the downstream fallback, not the OAuth root cause.

kpis.description: Percentage of active warehouse connections whose last sync completed with code 'ok' (failCount = 0). Checked by reviewing connection records for any project with a real (non-demo) provider.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Open the app as each eshop project, navigate to Katalog → Sklad, and check the connection badge status. Count connections showing a healthy (green) last-sync vs those showing an error or stale state. Report healthy / total."}
kpis.name: Warehouse provider sync success rate
kpis.rationale: A broken provider connection silently leaves the catalog stale, so ad spend continues running against incorrect stock levels until someone notices the badge.

kpis.description: Percentage of generated inventory budget moves that an operator accepts (state='accepted') vs all moves that have been acted on (accepted + dismissed), indicating whether the AI-generated action plan changes actual operator behaviour.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Open Sklad & sezónnost for each eshop project that has a saved plan. Count moves in 'accepted' state vs all moves in 'accepted' or 'dismissed' state. Report accepted / (accepted + dismissed); skip projects with all moves still 'proposed'."}
kpis.name: Inventory plan move acceptance rate
kpis.rationale: If operators dismiss or ignore most proposed moves the plan adds no value — this number tells whether the budget-rebalancing recommendations are credible enough to act on.

kpis.description: Percentage of local-type projects that have imported at least one live-data source (coverage, reviews, or GBP) via LocalSourcePanel rather than running on illustrative sample data.
kpis.name: Local live-signal adoption rate
kpis.rationale: If every local project stays on sample data, the rank matrix and gap table display fictional numbers — the module produces no real insights and any AI diagnosis is grounded in invented figures.

kpis.description: Percentage of identified service×locality coverage gaps (hasPage=false rows in the gap table) that an operator has toggled to hasPage=true via CoverageCell, indicating they have created or confirmed a landing page for that combination.
kpis.name: Coverage gap page-creation rate
kpis.rationale: The module's entire value proposition is driving local-page creation for uncovered service×area pairs; without this metric there is no signal that gap analysis is translating into actual operator action.

kpis.description: Percentage of leadgen/local projects that have replaced the illustrative sample with at least one real imported CRM lead (resolve.ts live=true path).
kpis.measure_config: {"steps":"Open each leadgen/local project's lead-quality funnel view; check whether the header reads 'reálná importovaná data z CRM' (live import) vs the sample label. Count live-import projects / total leadgen+local projects."}
kpis.name: Lead CRM import adoption rate
kpis.rationale: If the adoption rate is low, the entire funnel, CPQL alerts, and AI recap grounding are running on synthetic sample data — the subsystem is deployed but not doing its job.

kpis.description: Percentage of local-type projects that have at least one competitor saved in the competitor store, ensuring AI recap and social prompts receive comparative grounding context rather than an empty string.
kpis.measure_config: {"steps":["Open the app with LOCAL_DB=true and 3+ local-type projects seeded","For each project navigate to the Local SEO section and open the competitor panel","Count projects with ≥1 competitor entry vs. total local projects","Report filled / total * 100"]}
kpis.name: Competitor grounding fill rate
kpis.rationale: When the competitor set is empty, competitorGroundingText() returns '' and every AI recap and social output silently loses market-comparison context — the most distinctive value of the local SEO module.

kpis.description: Fraction of content tool invocations (article-draft, repurpose, social, comparison-outline) that return meta.partialDemo=true — where the model responded but one or more structural sections were silently replaced with canned templates.
kpis.name: Content partial-backfill rate
kpis.rationale: Partial backfill is the silent failure mode: the user receives real-looking output that is partly canned, no UI warning fires, and the existing 'LLM demo fallback rate' KPI misses it because that only tracks the full-demo case.

kpis.description: Of all SEO briefs generated in a project, the fraction that are subsequently used as input to an article-draft call in the same project within the same session or week.
kpis.name: Brief-to-draft pipeline completion rate
kpis.rationale: A brief that never becomes a draft is stalled content inventory; a low completion rate points to a workflow handoff gap between the two primary content tools, not a quality problem.

kpis.description: Among users with a Sklik connection, the percentage who have explicitly confirmed the haléře → CZK money-unit conversion via PATCH /api/campaigns/sklik. Unconfirmed connections display Sklik spend values 100× inflated on every campaigns screen.
kpis.measure_config: {"journey":"Sign in as a Sklik-connected test user whose halereConfirmed is false; open the campaigns page; verify the haléře-confirmation banner or prompt is visible; send PATCH /api/campaigns/sklik with {halereConfirmed:true}; verify the response carries connection.halereConfirmed=true and the prompt no longer appears on reload.","pass_condition":"Confirmation prompt displayed before PATCH; PATCH returns 200 with halereConfirmed:true; prompt absent after confirmation"}
kpis.name: Sklik haléře confirmation rate
kpis.rationale: An unconfirmed Sklik connection silently shows every cost figure 100× too high, making budget decisions and AI evaluations for that account structurally wrong.

kpis.description: % of drafts generated in 'auto' autonomy mode that are immediately auto-approved (model confidence high, no risks flagged) vs. queued as pending for human review
kpis.measure_config: {"journey":"In a project with at least one twin channel set to 'auto' autonomy, trigger 5 reply generations via the outbox; count the fraction that land with status 'approved' and autoApproved=true without any human action"}
kpis.name: Twin auto-approval rate
kpis.rationale: A near-zero auto-approval rate means the model always hedges — low confidence or inflated risks — so the autonomy gate provides no throughput benefit and users are manually reviewing every draft.

kpis.description: Percentage of active tenants who have saved ≥1 manually pinned or hand-written pattern in their patterns library (source: 'manual' or pinned auto-pattern in the patterns Firestore collection).
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Query the 'patterns' tenant-docs collection (or LOCAL_DB tenant_docs table for offline). Count tenants with ≥1 pattern doc vs. total active tenants. Report as a percentage."}
kpis.name: Pattern library pin adoption rate
kpis.rationale: Campaign evaluation grounding only compounds in value when users save lessons; a near-zero pin rate means the patterns library never builds institutional memory and every AI eval starts fresh from auto-mined samples alone.

kpis.description: Percentage of saved keyword lists whose source is 'google' or 'sklik' rather than the deterministic sample fallback
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Query the keyword lists store (SQLite: SELECT source, COUNT(*) FROM tenant_docs WHERE collection='keywordLists' GROUP BY source; Firestore: aggregate over keywordLists collection). Compute (google_count + sklik_count) / total * 100."}
kpis.name: Keyword live-data rate
kpis.rationale: When this is near zero every project receives identical seeded ideas instead of real market intelligence, making the keyword engine cosmetic rather than competitive.

kpis.description: Percentage of Výkon section loads — on projects with ≥14 days of data (coverage = 'full') — where InsightsPanel renders at least one insight line.
kpis.measure_config: {"steps":"1. Open Výkon for 5 projects that each have ≥14 days of campaign data synced. 2. Count how many show ≥1 item in the 'Co stojí za pozornost' panel. 3. Rate = passing / 5."}
kpis.name: Výkon insight fill rate
kpis.rationale: A blank panel on a full-coverage project is the section's silent failure — users see no automated signal and typically assume nothing is actionable rather than suspecting a data or threshold issue.

kpis.description: Percentage of campaign-eligible projects (type = eshop, app, leadgen, or local) that have `adsCustomerId` set.
kpis.measure_config: {"instruction":"Query the projects store (Firestore or local SQLite). Count projects where type IN ('eshop','app','leadgen','local'). Of those, count the subset with a non-null, non-empty adsCustomerId. Divide and multiply by 100."}
kpis.name: Ads account link rate
kpis.rationale: Without a linked Google Ads account the campaigns, performance, and live-report modules show no data — the project's core value prop is silent.

kpis.description: Share of upsertCampaigns writes that set degraded=true (connector could not reach the ad platform and fell back to sample data).
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Query the Firestore tenants collection (or LOCAL_DB campaign_docs table, collection __root__) for the degraded field; count docs where degraded==true over the last 7 days divided by total synced docs in the same window."}
kpis.name: Degraded campaign sync rate
kpis.rationale: A degraded sync silently stores sample data under the live label; even a handful of affected tenants see fabricated numbers on their Výkon dashboard without any error surfaced to them.

kpis.description: Percentage of projects with live campaign data that have triggered at least one campaign evaluation in the last 30 days
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Identify projects with synced campaign data (non-demo). Of those, check AI dispatch logs (src/app/api/ai/dispatch.ts, mode=campaign-eval) to count which project IDs appeared in the last 30 days. Report active-eval projects ÷ total projects with live campaign data."}
kpis.name: Campaign eval run rate
kpis.rationale: Campaign eval is the AI layer that converts raw Sklik/Google data into a scored action plan — a low run rate means the most consultative AI feature is invisible to its target users.

kpis.description: Percentage of closed months where the GoalPacing mid-month projection (at day ≥15, probabilityReliable=true) landed within ±15% of the actual final month revenue.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"At the start of each month, compare the prior month's day-15 pacing.projection value (stored or recalled from PerformanceData snapshot) against the month-end actual revenue. Count months within ±15% band divided by all closed months with a reliable mid-month forecast."}
kpis.name: Goal pacing forecast accuracy rate
kpis.rationale: If the pacing forecast is systematically wrong, users stop trusting the GoalPacing card and the goalProbability figure becomes noise — the core value-add of this widget evaporates silently.

kpis.description: Percentage of real (non-demo) image generation runs where the winning candidate carries a genuine Gemini vision score (scored=true), meaning the winner was quality-ranked rather than crowned arbitrarily.
kpis.measure_config: {"expected":"Winner has scored=true on ≥90% of runs","steps":["Trigger a live image generation (LEONARDO_API_KEY present)","Inspect the StudioResult returned by generateImageSet","Check that images.find(i => i.winner).scored === true"]}
kpis.name: Image vision-score rate
kpis.rationale: When Gemini vision is unavailable the studio silently crowns an arbitrary candidate and marks it scored=false — users receive no quality guarantee and the defect is invisible without this check.

kpis.description: Percentage of saved creative links (creativeAttribution collection) that have non-null metrics, indicating the revenue-feedback loop actually has signal for getStylePrior to learn from.
kpis.measure_config: {"expected":"≥50% of creative links carry at least one revenue metric","steps":["List documents in tenants/{tenant}/creativeAttribution","Count rows where metrics is non-null","Divide by total rows"]}
kpis.name: Creative attribution fill rate
kpis.rationale: If attribution metrics are never written back, getStylePrior returns no signal and every generation ignores the best-earning style — the system's core learning loop is inert.

kpis.description: At end-of-UTC-day, the fraction of the global daily spend ceiling (AI_GLOBAL_DAILY_CEILING) still unused. Computed as (ceiling - used) / ceiling from the Firestore `ratelimits/_global_YYYY-MM-DD` doc that durableGuard writes.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"In Firebase console (or via admin script), open ratelimits/_global_{today} and read `count` and compare to AI_GLOBAL_DAILY_CEILING env. Headroom = (ceiling - count) / ceiling * 100."}
kpis.name: Global AI ceiling headroom rate
kpis.rationale: When the ceiling empties before end of day every subsequent paid AI call returns a hard 429 until UTC midnight — a cliff that no spend-dollar metric signals in advance.

kpis.description: Fraction of ad experiments (tenants/*/experiments/*) where winnerVariantId is non-null, meaning at least one variant has had real performance metrics written back via updateVariantMetrics.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"In Firebase console, query each tenant's experiments sub-collection; count docs where winnerVariantId != null divided by total experiment docs."}
kpis.name: A/B experiment winner convergence rate
kpis.rationale: An experiment without metrics never produces a winner; if operators aren't feeding CTR or conversion data back, the A/B framework is purely decorative and ad copy quality stagnates.

kpis.description: Share of AI-generated RSA sets that score ≥65 (rating: good or excellent) by the ad-strength heuristic on first generation, before any manual edits.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Run the PPC ad generator for 10 representative projects, record the ad-strength score displayed immediately after generation (before editing), and compute the fraction where rating is 'good' or 'excellent' (score ≥ 65)."}
kpis.name: Ad strength 'good or better' rate
kpis.rationale: The ad-strength heuristic is the quality gate between generation and launch; a rate below 70% means the AI regularly produces copy users must heavily edit before exporting.

kpis.description: Percentage of active projects whose latest stored recap (any period) is non-stale — i.e. the stored inputHash still matches the current data digest when the report page loads.
kpis.measure_config: {"journey":"Open the /app/[project]/reporty page for a sample of 5+ active projects; check whether the 'stale' banner appears on the most-recent recap for any period. Currency rate = projects with no stale latest recap ÷ projects checked."}
kpis.name: Recap currency rate
kpis.rationale: A stale recap means the user paid for an AI summary that silently no longer reflects their numbers — the core promise of the recaps module is broken.

kpis.description: Percentage of scheduled crons whose most-recent recorded run completed with ok: true, as reported by GET /api/health.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"GET /api/health with Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET; read crons[]; compute count(ok=true) / count(crons) * 100. Flag any cron in cronsStale separately."}
kpis.name: Cron run success rate
kpis.rationale: A cron recorded as ok:false has silently dropped deliveries for some tenants — this is the earliest warning that the scheduler is malfunctioning beyond what timing-only checks catch.

kpis.description: Percentage of weekly digest sends where the insight brief was sourced from the client's real synced data (live=true) rather than sample placeholders.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"After each weekly digest cron run, check the run record results[]; count entries where isLive=true vs total entries that included an insights section. Sample size: last 4 weekly runs."}
kpis.name: Digest live-data rate
kpis.rationale: Clients receiving sample-data insights in their weekly email get no real business signal — this rate exposes whether the sync→digest pipeline is silently failing upstream.

kpis.description: % of users with an active BYOM vendor who generated at least one AI output routed through their own key in the past 7 days — distinct from key activation, which only measures key storage.
kpis.measure_config: {"steps":["Sign in as a BYOM-plan test account that has an active vendor set","Trigger one AI operation (e.g. campaign content generation)","Verify via LightTrack logs that the operation hit the user's vendor endpoint, not the app's env key","Aggregate weekly across known BYOM-plan accounts: (accounts with ≥1 BYOM-routed op) / (accounts with activeVendor set) × 100"]}
kpis.name: BYOM routing utilization rate
kpis.rationale: The gap between activation and routing reveals whether users trust BYOM enough to rely on it day-to-day; a wide gap signals the settings UI adds keys but nothing in the product closes the loop.

kpis.description: Percentage of active projects where the monthly report is grounded in live Google Ads data (report_metrics.meta.source = 'google-ads') rather than the sample spine.
kpis.measure_config: {"cmd":"sqlite3 .data/systedo.db \"SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN json_extract(data,'$.meta.source')='google-ads' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) FROM report_metrics LEFT JOIN projects ON projects.id = report_metrics.project_id;\"","parse":"first numeric token"}
kpis.name: Live report adoption rate
kpis.rationale: The live Ads path is the premium experience — a low rate means most clients are looking at sample numbers and the sync investment is going unused.

kpis.description: Share of all generateStructured calls in the week that fell all the way to the deterministic demo (demo: true in llmTelemetry) — meaning every configured provider was either unavailable or exhausted — leaving users with fabricated placeholder content they cannot distinguish from real AI output.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Open the admin LLM telemetry dashboard (or query Firestore llmTelemetry for the week): count docs where demo=true, divide by total docs for the week, multiply by 100."}
kpis.name: LLM demo fallback rate
kpis.rationale: A spike here means every AI feature is silently serving fake data — the hardest outage to notice from outside because no error is thrown.

kpis.description: Share of real (non-demo) generateStructured calls in the week where the parsed response was classified as corrupt (status: 'corrupt' in llmTelemetry) — meaning the model returned valid JSON that was nonetheless missing more than a third of the schema's required fields.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"In the admin LLM telemetry dashboard (or Firestore llmTelemetry): filter demo=false for the week, count status='corrupt', divide by total non-demo docs, multiply by 100."}
kpis.name: LLM corrupt output rate
kpis.rationale: Corrupt calls register as successes but produce AI content with blank or missing fields; users see broken output while metrics show green.

kpis.description: Total estimated USD cost (sum of estCostUsd across non-dev Gemini and BYOM calls recorded in llmTelemetry for the week) — the operator's direct API bill for the gateway.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"In the admin LLM telemetry dashboard (or Firestore llmTelemetry): sum estCostUsd for all docs in the past 7 days where demo=false."}
kpis.name: Weekly LLM API spend
kpis.rationale: Unexpected spend spikes expose runaway repair loops, prompt bloat, or BYOM misconfiguration before the monthly cloud invoice arrives.

kpis.description: Percentage of active projects where listOfferings returns a non-null result, meaning the user has committed at least one real offering to the store rather than running purely on the type-specific seed catalog.
kpis.measure_config: {"steps":["Open the app as a test operator","For a sample of ≥10 active projects spanning all types (eshop, app, leadgen, local), navigate to the project catalog page","Check whether each project's catalog reflects user-saved data (source !== seed, or updatedAt reflects a user action) or is purely the seed fallback","Record saved_projects / total_projects as the rate"]}
kpis.name: Catalog saved-over-seed rate
kpis.rationale: If projects never graduate from seeds, every dependent module (inventory, ad copy, local SEO matrix) runs on demo data — the whole Offering spine delivers no real business grounding.

kpis.description: Percentage of active catalog SKUs in saved catalogs that have persisted AI-written ad copy (source: 'ai' in composeCatalogAdCopy), versus relying solely on the deterministic floor fallback.
kpis.measure_config: {"steps":["For a sample of active projects with saved catalogs, open the catalog ad-copy module","Count total active SKUs across the sample","Count SKUs where StoredAdCopy exists in the ad-copy store (demo === false preferred, but any stored entry counts)","Report stored_skus / total_skus"]}
kpis.name: Ad copy SKU coverage rate
kpis.rationale: The ad-copy-store was built to fix the 'generate 500 times' UX failure — if SKU coverage stays near 0%, users are either not discovering the feature or the batch generation path is broken.

kpis.description: Percentage of active projects that have a real monthly revenue goal configured (sanitizeProjectGoal returns non-null) rather than relying on the illustrative sample goal.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Open 10 randomly sampled active projects in the app; for each, navigate to the goals/report configuration surface and check whether a real goal value is displayed or the label 'ukázkový cíl' appears. Count projects with a real goal / total checked."}
kpis.name: Revenue goal set rate
kpis.rationale: When no real goal is saved the pacing and attainment surfaces in the report show a fabricated sample target — the primary purpose of the goals subsystem is unused and the operator cannot judge campaign performance against an actual business target.

kpis.description: Percentage of projects with a cost model that include at least one of monthlyOverhead or perOrderCost — the fields that activate the overhead-loaded break-even and true net-profit paths.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Open 10 randomly sampled projects that have any cost model saved; inspect the cost-model editor for each and check whether monthlyOverhead or perOrderCost is non-zero. Count projects with at least one field > 0 / total with a cost model."}
kpis.name: Loaded cost model adoption rate
kpis.rationale: A cost model with only grossMarginPct produces gross break-even (identical to pre-model behavior); the loaded break-even and true net-profit computation — the core value proposition of the cost-model subsystem — is only reached when overhead or per-order cost is present.

kpis.description: % of persisted diagnoses (across all three kinds: cohort, lead-source, local) that have been moved to `resolved` status out of the total stored. Measures whether operators are completing the status lifecycle rather than letting findings accumulate as `new`.
kpis.measure_config: {"journey":"Open the diagnosis panel for a project that has stored diagnoses. Count items in each status bucket visible in the history strip. Compute resolved / total × 100."}
kpis.name: Diagnosis resolution rate
kpis.rationale: If diagnoses pile up as `new` the engine is generating AI spend with zero downstream action — this rate is the earliest signal that the feedback loop is broken.

kpis.description: Of resolved diagnoses that carry a Direction-1 key-metric snapshot, % where `compareOutcome` returns `improved` (key metric moved ≥5 % relative in the right direction since the diagnosis was filed). The three tracked metrics are worst-cohort LTV:CAC, lead-source qualification rate, and local coverage %.
kpis.measure_config: {"journey":"For a project with at least 3 resolved diagnoses that have outcome chips: count the chips showing 'improved' vs 'unchanged'/'worse'. Compute improved / (total with chips) × 100."}
kpis.name: Diagnosis outcome improvement rate
kpis.rationale: This is the engine's ultimate value claim — that acting on a diagnosis moves the needle; without this metric there is no evidence the AI recommendations are worth anything.

kpis.description: Percentage of live projects where the user has entered actual revenue and ad spend for at least one period, overriding the estimated channel data in the profit view.
kpis.measure_config: {"check":"Query finance-inputs store: count projects where realNumbers is non-empty object divided by total projects with profit module active."}
kpis.name: Real-numbers reconciliation adoption rate
kpis.rationale: Without real-number overrides every margin figure is estimated; if most users never enter their books the module is surfacing fiction as insight.

kpis.description: Percentage of live projects where 'Apply to report' has been used at least once, writing the profit module's blended margin and overhead to the shared cost model.
kpis.measure_config: {"check":"Query cost-model store: count projects with a saved grossMarginPct that matches the profit module's last-posted value, divided by projects with both the profit module and a monthly report active."}
kpis.name: Profit-to-report sync rate
kpis.rationale: When this rate is low, users see two different profit numbers in two tabs — the reconciliation UX (ReconcileNote) is failing to drive the fix-action it exists to prompt.

kpis.description: Percentage of profit module users who have saved at least one named scenario for side-by-side comparison.
kpis.measure_config: {"check":"Query finance-inputs store: count projects where scenarios array length > 0 divided by total projects with finance-inputs record."}
kpis.name: Margin scenario save rate
kpis.rationale: Scenario planning is the module's highest-value differentiator; if nobody saves a scenario the 'co kdyby' simulator is dead weight and usage is purely passive.

kpis.description: Percentage of active projects that have at least one channel voice trained (source='trained') rather than the factory sample — checked by visiting each project's twin state page and reading the ReadinessRibbon / voice-studio current-voice panel.
kpis.measure_config: {"aggregate":"trained_count / total_active_projects * 100","steps":["Open /app for each active project","Navigate to the Twin module","Check whether TwinVoiceStudio shows a trained voice (pill says 'hlas trénován …') on any scope","Record trained vs sample-only"]}
kpis.name: Twin voice training adoption rate
kpis.rationale: A twin that was never trained drafts in a generic sample register on every channel — low adoption means the core value proposition (brand-voice AI) is simply not in use.

kpis.description: Percentage of proposed change-sets (status: pending) that are subsequently approved and applied, versus those left pending or that fail.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Count change-sets with status='applied' in a rolling 30-day window. Divide by total change-sets created in the same window (excluding those still pending at measurement time)."}
kpis.name: Change-set approval rate
kpis.rationale: A low approval rate means proposals are generated but not trusted — the simulation or guardrail experience is failing to give operators enough confidence to act.

kpis.description: Percentage of applied change-sets that are subsequently reverted within 7 days of application.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Count change-sets reaching status='reverted' within 7 days of their applied timestamp. Divide by total change-sets that reached 'applied' in the same 30-day window."}
kpis.name: Change-set revert rate
kpis.rationale: High revert rates signal that the pre-apply simulation is overstating projected impact and operators are being misled into applying moves that hurt real spend.

kpis.description: Percentage of anonymous sessions that land on /app (triggering AppSignInGate) and successfully complete Google OAuth within the same session.
kpis.measure_config: {"procedure":"Open /app in a fresh incognito window; confirm the gate renders with the value-prop card; click 'Sign in with Google'; verify OAuth redirect completes and the authed shell loads at the original pathname. Pass = full round-trip succeeds without error. Repeat weekly or after any auth dependency change."}
kpis.name: Sign-in gate conversion rate
kpis.rationale: AppSignInGate is the single conversion wall between a public visitor and an authenticated workspace; a broken or degraded flow silently kills every downstream activation metric.

kpis.description: Percentage of newly created projects where the AI website-scan completes, the project profile is seeded, and the user subsequently opens the dashboard — the activation event that proves the core value loop is accessible to a new user.
kpis.measure_config: {"instruction":"In PostHog (or equivalent), build a funnel: Project Created → onboarding_scan_complete event → /app/[projectId] dashboard viewed. Report the % reaching the final step, cohorted by week of sign-up."}
kpis.name: Onboarding activation rate
kpis.rationale: If new users don't reach their first seeded dashboard, every downstream KPI is irrelevant — this is the gate the whole product stands behind.

kpis.description: Percentage of all created projects that record at least one AI generation or dashboard view in the preceding 7-day window — confirms the product is used at the natural weekly-review cadence rather than abandoned after onboarding.
kpis.measure_config: {"instruction":"In PostHog, compute distinct project IDs with any ai_generation_complete or dashboard_viewed event in the past 7 days, divided by total non-deleted projects. Report weekly."}
kpis.name: Weekly returning project rate
kpis.rationale: Adamant is explicitly a weekly-cadence tool; if projects go dark between onboarding and churning the core value loop is broken regardless of how many accounts exist.

kpis.description: Percentage of AI-generated assets (ad copy variants, articles, social posts) that are exported, copied, or pushed to a connected channel within 7 days of generation — the completion signal that the generate half of the value loop lands in real campaigns.
kpis.measure_config: {"instruction":"In PostHog, count asset_exported or post_published events within 7 days of a matching ai_generation_complete event, divided by total ai_generation_complete events in the cohort period."}
kpis.name: AI content publish rate
kpis.rationale: Generated content that is never published means the triage step works but the payoff doesn't — this distinguishes a demo toy from a real workflow tool.

kpis.description: Median minutes from project creation to the first AI-generated asset (any of: ad copy variant, article draft, social post, keyword cluster) — measures how quickly a new user reaches tangible value without requiring manual data entry.
kpis.measure_config: {"instruction":"In PostHog, compute the median time delta between project_created and the first ai_generation_complete event per user cohort. Exclude demo/seed projects."}
kpis.name: Median time-to-first-asset
kpis.rationale: The onboarding scan is the speed-to-value differentiator; if the scan-to-asset path takes longer than a coffee break, users don't return to verify the asset.

kpis.description: Percentage of active projects (at least one campaign-view in the past 30 days) whose Google Ads or Sklik campaign data was synced within the preceding 24 hours — ensures the 'correct performance read' the product promises is actually current.
kpis.measure_config: {"instruction":"Query the campaigns_snapshots table (Firestore or SQLite) for active projects. Count those where max(synced_at) > NOW()-24h, divide by total active projects. Run weekly and enter result here."}
kpis.name: Campaign data freshness rate
kpis.rationale: A performance read off stale data is worse than no data — users make budget decisions on it; freshness is a trust invariant, not an infrastructure nicety.

kpis.description: Percentage of LLM generation requests hitting /api/ai that return an error to the caller (model timeout, rate-limit exhaustion, JSON parse failure, or slot-acquisition failure) over the trailing 7 days.
kpis.measure_config: {"connector":"sentry","instruction":"Fetch error events tagged to the /api/ai route in the past 7 days. Divide by total transaction count for the same route and period. Express as a percentage."}
kpis.name: AI dispatch error rate
kpis.rationale: Every AI dispatch error is a failed generate attempt that breaks the value loop; at the rate limits and quotas in place a spike here is the first signal of a systemic LLM issue.

kpis.description: Percentage of accounts that activate at least one BYOM provider key (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, or OpenRouter) within 30 days of account creation — a leading indicator that power users find enough value to commit real API spend.
kpis.measure_config: {"instruction":"In PostHog, compute the 30-day cohort funnel: account_created → byom_key_saved. Report the conversion rate by sign-up week. Alternatively query the byom_keys table for accounts created in the period and check for non-null key entries."}
kpis.name: BYOM key activation rate
kpis.rationale: BYOM adoption is the clearest revealed-preference signal: users who wire in their own API keys have bet real money that the product replaces manual work.

kpis.description: Percentage of Pro-tier projects that receive their scheduled AI-generated weekly performance digest within 2 hours of the scheduled cron window — confirms the autonomous reporting loop the Pro tier is sold on actually runs.
kpis.measure_config: {"instruction":"Query the cron execution log (cron_runs table or Vercel Cron logs) for the weekly digest job. Count successful completions per eligible Pro project, divide by total expected runs for the period. Enter the resulting rate."}
kpis.name: Weekly digest on-time delivery rate
kpis.rationale: The weekly digest is the Pro tier's primary retention hook — a missed digest is a missed renewal argument and an invisible reliability failure the user only notices when they stop hearing from the product.
